name: Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptor 1-Related Hypophosphatemic Rickets

criteria.description: Evidence of renal phosphate wasting with hypophosphatemia
Identification of pathogenic FGFR1 mutation by genetic testing
Clinical and radiological signs of rickets or osteomalacia
Normal serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels
Elevated circulating fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of renal phosphate wasting, clinical/radiological evidence of rickets or osteomalacia, and identification of a pathogenic FGFR1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; biochemical findings support clinical suspicion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypophosphatemia due to renal phosphate wasting
Rickets with metaphyseal cupping and fraying
Osteomalacia with bone pain and deformities

common.symptomName: Lower limb bowing (genu varum or valgum)

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to electrolyte imbalance

laboratory: Hypophosphatemia with low tubular maximum reabsorption of phosphate (TmP/GFR)
Normal serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels
imaging: Radiographs showing metaphyseal cupping, fraying, and widening
Bone demineralization and osteomalacia on X-ray
genetic: Pathogenic variants in FGFR1 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Dental abnormalities including enamel hypoplasia and abscesses
Growth retardation documented by anthropometric measurements

distinguishingFeatures: Mutation in PHEX gene instead of FGFR1
Similar biochemical profile but different genetic cause
Caused by mutations in FGF23 gene
Elevated FGF23 but no FGFR1 mutation
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

redFlags: Severe hypophosphatemia refractory to standard vitamin D therapy
Early onset of rickets symptoms in infancy or early childhood
references: Carpenter TO. The expanding family of hypophosphatemic syndromes. J Bone Miner Metab. 2012;30(1):1-9.
Imel EA, Econs MJ. Fibroblast growth factor 23 and hypophosphatemic disorders. J Bone Miner Res. 2005;20(9):1547-1552.
